findings.title: Ram damage still runs in the single-ship flight paths, which have no stepRocks and no born-mask reset
findings.claim: §3.1 says stepFlight and stepSoloFlight never wake a rock and use the kind-1 rule of §5.1. But §5.1 applies ram damage in 'any of the three cases', so a ram at 30 < vc ≤ 40 still damages a static rock in those paths and can break it if it is cracked. The break writes kind-2 pieces that never move there, because neither path calls stepRocks. It also sets born flags that are never cleared, because the mask is cleared only at the start of stepDuel. Every later ship contact then skips those slots for good.
findings.evidence: spec L60-L64 (born mask cleared per stepDuel tick), L65-L67 (flight paths: no wake), L192-L195 (ram damage in any of the three cases); physics.ts:L67-L71 (stepFlight: resolveContacts only), L75-L79 (stepSoloFlight: hitStatics only)
findings.why: It changes rock state in the dev flight view and the §4 flight tests, which the change was meant to leave as today. It also leaves pieces frozen in place and permanently uncollidable.
findings.fix: State that in stepFlight and stepSoloFlight a rock contact is exactly today's hitStatic: no ram damage, no break and no born-mask use. Or say that those paths clear the born mask at their start and also run stepRocks.

findings.title: missileLaunch admission no longer matches what happens when a rockLock(torpedo) arrives in the same tick
findings.claim: step.ts admits missileLaunch with canLaunch against the state before folding (step.ts:L187). §6.4 makes canLaunch test the rock's distance while torpRock ≥ 0, and a same-tick rockLock(torpedo, k) sets torpRock only later, in applyWeaponsInput. Admission therefore uses the old target (the ship, or the old rock) while applyWeaponsInput's canLaunch uses the new rock. The result can say 'applied' when nothing launches, or 'unavailable' when the auto-launch fires that same tick. The step's own comment requires every result to match what happens (step.ts:L174-L176).
findings.evidence: spec L214-L220 (rockLock validated, then folded later), L254-L258 (range and launch by torpRock); step.ts:L174-L176, L179-L189; weapons.ts:L43-L54, L176-L180
findings.why: Command results go to clients. A mismatched result breaks the existing admission-equals-effect contract and gives the UI wrong feedback. Two implementers could also 'fix' it differently: by pre-applying the torpRock for admission, or not.
findings.fix: Specify that missileLaunch admission evaluates canLaunch with this tick's accepted rockLock(torpedo) already applied (the effective torpRock: the last accepted rockLock(torpedo) this tick, else the stored value). Alternatively, say that the result may differ and why.

findings.title: rocksBroken can count one break twice when an overflow piece turns to dust
findings.claim: §8 adds 1 to rocksBroken for every split or dust event of a rock's break whose ship is that ship. A crew-caused break where the pool is full and no eviction victim exists gives a split event plus a dust event for each piece that had no slot (§3.4 'otherwise the new piece is dust'). The spec does not say whether those overflow dusts carry ship, or whether they count. One break could therefore add 1, 2 or 3.
findings.evidence: spec L129-L132 (overflow piece becomes dust, every dust emits an event), L314-L320 (ship field; rocksBroken +1 per split or dust event)
findings.why: rocksBroken is hashed. A near-full pool is the expected stress state, so twin implementations would diverge.
findings.fix: Define rocksBroken as +1 per break, whatever the number of events. Or state that overflow-piece dust events carry no ship and do not count, as eviction dust does not.

findings.title: §9.4 piece floor is met by the direct hit alone
findings.claim: The 10 largest belt rocks are close to r 45, so all of them are above the new burst threshold of 35. The direct hit alone gives 6 pieces (rp about 16, above ROCK_MIN_R). The 'at least 6 pieces' floor therefore says nothing about secondary breaks; only the collision floor tests anything.
findings.evidence: spec L110-L111 (belt r 15 to 45), L118-L120 (r ≥ 35: 6 pieces), L343-L347 (floor: at least 6 pieces)
findings.why: The proxy was revised so that it would no longer be trivially true, and the piece floor still is.
findings.fix: Raise the piece floor above 6 (for example at least 8, so that one secondary break is needed). Or say plainly that the piece floor only checks the burst and the collision floor carries the chain test.

findings.title: A laser shot whose first blocker is a born slot, and a manual shot with an off-target rock lock, are not described
findings.claim: §3.4 skips damage on born slots, but it does not say whether firstBlocker skips a born slot or stops on it. An earlier ship's shot this tick can make a born piece on the later ship's line, and the answer decides whether the shot continues to the enemy line or another rock. Separately, with laserRock ≥ 0 and the rock off target, the spec does not say what a manual press hits: today's laserRockTarget uses the enemy line or the nose ray.
findings.why: Both cases are rare and resolve to some deterministic code path, but the two rules leave room for different readings.
findings.fix: Say that firstBlocker skips born slots (the line passes through them). Say that a manual shot with an off-target rock lock follows today's miss path (the enemy line or the nose ray).
